policy_title: Scrap Illegal Migration Act and Rwanda Scheme, Uphold Refugee Convention
stated: Scrap the Conservatives’ Illegal Migration Act and their Rwanda scheme, uphold the Refugee Convention, and provide safe and legal routes to sanctuary for refugees, helping to prevent dangerous Channel crossings. Cancel the Conservatives’ unworkable Rwanda scheme and invest the savings in clearing the asylum backlog.

source.quote: Scrap the Conservatives’ Illegal Migration Act and their Rwanda scheme, uphold the Refugee Convention, and provide safe and legal routes to sanctuary for refugees, helping to prevent dangerous Channel crossings. Cancel the Conservatives’ unworkable Rwanda scheme and invest the savings in clearing the asylum backlog.

bearing_set.reason: Scrapping the Illegal Migration Act directly restores due-process and legal-rights protections for asylum seekers; upholding the Refugee Convention is explicitly about the legal-rights framework governing refugee status and equal treatment — squarely within O9's scope.

Scrapping a deterrence mechanism (Rwanda/IMA) is contested on border-security grounds, while redirecting savings to clear the asylum backlog directly affects justice-system throughput — both indicators under O5.
The Illegal Migration Act contained extended administrative detention powers; scrapping it reduces state coercive power over asylum seekers, a direct O10 liberty indicator.

The Rwanda scheme has cost hundreds of millions (with negligible operational output); cancellation has a real fiscal saving, though redirecting it to backlog clearance is also expenditure — the net effect on the debt/funded-spending path is non-negligible and genuinely contested.

membership_note: Four fundamentals earn real verdicts: justice/security (O5, contested); due process and refugee protections (O9, improves); detention-power reduction (O10, improves); and the fiscal saving vs. backlog-investment tradeoff (O12, contested). O15 cohesion and O13 prosperity effects are too indirect and mechanistically underspecified to clear the non-negligible bar.
